description: Public maturity tracker for AI-era human–AI decision research. Stage reflects project artifacts, not scientific certainty.

stageDefinitions.idea: A falsifiable research question with related established concepts, but no project protocol yet.
stageDefinitions.protocol: A reproducible comparison protocol is published. No project result is implied.
stageDefinitions.experiment: A preregistered or otherwise documented run exists with model/task/sample metadata, but results are not yet promoted to a finding.
stageDefinitions.result: A project result is published with methods, raw or summary data, uncertainty and limitations.
stageDefinitions.replication: The result has been repeated across a meaningfully different sample, task, model or independent group.

interpretationRule: Never infer a later stage from external papers alone. External evidence can motivate a track, but project stages advance only when the corresponding project artifact exists.

entries.name: AI Anchoring Loop
entries.nextMilestone: Run the protocol with a predefined task set and publish model/version, anchor values, sample size and uncertainty.
entries.whyItMatters: AI can become the first numerical reference before a person has formed an independent estimate.

entries.name: Sycophancy Reinforcement Loop
entries.nextMilestone: Separate model agreement from human confidence and test neutral, preference-signalling and counterevidence conditions.
entries.whyItMatters: An agreeable answer can be mistaken for independent support for a view the user already signalled.

entries.name: Cognitive Offloading Debt
entries.nextMilestone: Run an immediate-quality plus delayed-retention comparison rather than measuring task completion alone.
entries.whyItMatters: Faster completion and durable understanding are different outcomes.

entries.name: Source-Memory Blur
entries.nextMilestone: Measure delayed source attribution for human-only, AI-only and mixed creation conditions.
entries.whyItMatters: Mixed workflows may make it harder to remember whether an idea came from the person, a source or the model.

entries.name: Synthetic Consensus Illusion
entries.nextMilestone: Publish a protocol comparing several apparently independent AI answers with the same answers plus source-lineage disclosure.
entries.whyItMatters: Several generated answers may feel like independent confirmation even when their information lineage overlaps.

entries.name: Confidence Transfer
entries.nextMilestone: Publish a protocol holding answer quality constant while varying certainty language and objective calibration information.
entries.whyItMatters: Confident wording may change human reliance even when the underlying evidence does not improve.
